title: Safety in Industry
description: This course emphasizes Cal/OSHA (California General Industrial Safety Orders) standards and benefits of accident prevention. Students gain an understanding of personal protective clothing and equipment; industrial housekeeping; and safety when handling and storing materials, tools, and equipment. The implications of accidents--such as loss of productivity, morale, and real and intangible costs relating to accidents--are also discussed.
outcomes: Develop an awareness of potential safety hazards at home and the work site.
Compare and describe safety implementation programs in various work locations.
Prepare a safety inspection format and conduct a safety inspection of an operational facility.
Identify the immediate and recurring costs due to accidents.
Understand basic first aid procedures to administer at the scene of an accident.
content: The Supervisors role in promoting safety in the workplace
Costs associated with accidents/accident prevention Inspections
Safety in the workplace related to alcohol and drug problems.
Safety when handling and storing materials and tools
assignments: Scholarly journals and industry materials as chosen by instructor
Project and Oral Presentation: Prepare a strategic safety plan for an existing
business as it relates to the course content. The safety plans must detail Cal/OSHA
Injury Illness Prevention Plan. Report this safety plan with an oral presentation.
Write a personal safety plan that demonstrates your understanding of what safety
is at home, college, or workplace.
